stages.name: Foundations
stages.description: Script, pronunciation, basic vocabulary, greetings, numbers, family, daily life.

lessons.title: Meet Urdu
learning_goals: Recognize that Urdu letters change shape when joining

cards.urdu: اردو دائیں سے بائیں لکھی جاتی ہے۔
cards.roman: Urdu dayen se baen likhi jati hai.
cards.english: Urdu is written right to left.

cards.instruction: Swipe to indicate the direction Urdu is read.

lessons.title: Alphabet Part 1 (18 core letters)
learning_goals: Learn first 18 Urdu letters and sounds

cards.instruction: Apply the correct vowel to form 'با'

objectives: Understand how Urdu letters connect in initial, medial and final forms

cards.content: In Urdu, most letters connect from both sides, but some only connect from one side.

cards.question: Which letter does NOT connect from both sides?

objectives: Blend letters into basic two-letter combinations
Identify initial and final forms in reading
Read simple words with common letters
Distinguish between connecting vs non-connecting middle letters
Understand short vs long vowel influence in reading
Recognize short vowel pronunciation without diacritics

cards.content: Short vowels (zabar, zer, pesh) are often omitted in everyday Urdu writing.

objectives: Pronounce aspirated consonants like بھ، پھ، تھ، ٹھ، جھ correctly
Differentiate between aspirated vs non-aspirated sounds

cards.content: Do-Chashmi Heh (ھ) adds an air-burst to consonants, similar to the 'h' in 'pot-hold'.

cards.question: Which is the aspirated form of 'ب'?

objectives: Identify retroflex letters and their tongue position
Pronounce ٹ, ڈ, ڑ with proper curling of the tongue
Distinguish retroflex from dentals (ت، د، ر)

cards.content: Retroflex consonants are pronounced by curling the tongue backward, unlike English.

objectives: Recognize and pronounce deep guttural consonants
Differentiate soft vs harsh throat sounds
Read simple words containing خ، غ، ق correctly

cards.content: These letters come from the throat and have no direct English equivalents.

cards.question: Which word contains the deep 'q' sound?

objectives: Differentiate soft vs hard variations of similar letters

cards.content: Urdu has pairs like س/ص, ہ/ح, ز/ذ/ض/ظ that sound similar in modern speech but differ in writing.

cards.question: Which pair is pronounced the same in modern Urdu?

objectives: Blend aspirated, retroflex and deep-throat sounds into real words
Read beginner-level sentences containing new sounds
Build early fluency in sound recognition

cards.english: The child is picking a flower.

cards.question: Which sentence contains an aspirated sound?

objectives: Learn standard Islamic greetings used in Urdu

cards.content: السلام علیکم is the most common greeting in Urdu, meaning 'Peace be upon you'.

cards.english: And peace be upon you too

turns.english: And peace be upon you too

cards.question: What is the correct response to 'السلام علیکم'?

cards.content: 'آپ' is used formally (elders, strangers). 'تم' is informal (friends, younger people).

cards.english: How are you? (to a man, formal)
How are you? (to a woman, formal)

cards.content: To introduce yourself, use: میرا نام ___ ہے

cards.question: How do you say: 'My name is Ali'?

lessons.lesson_name: Mini Conversations: Putting It All Together
objectives: Hold a basic conversation in Urdu

turns.english: And peace be upon you too.

cards.urdu: میرا نام سارا ہے اور میں ٹھیک ہوں۔
cards.roman: mera naam Sara hai aur main theek hoon.
cards.english: My name is Sara and I am fine.

goals: Ask and answer the most common wh-questions
Build confidence with daily conversational patterns

phrases.urdu: آپ کس سے بات کر رہے ہیں؟
phrases.roman: Aap kis se baat kar rahe hain?

points: Urdu question structure: WH-word → subject → verb
"Kya" can appear at beginning (what) or end (yes/no question)
"Kaun" used for people — acts as subject
"Kis" changes meaning depending on context: kis ka, kis se, kis ko

goals: Build first verb structure (I am doing...)

forms.urdu: میں کر رہا ہوں / رہی ہوں

goals: Talk about hunger, taste, and liking/disliking

phrases.english: Please add a little more salt.
What would you like to eat?

notes: Food terms are gendered; many end with ی/ا

lines.english: What would you like to eat?

translate_to_urdu: What would you like to eat?

goals: Use 'there is / there are' in Urdu

phrases.english: There is a stove in the kitchen.

phrases.urdu: میں کمرہ صاف کر رہا ہوں۔
phrases.roman: Main kamra saaf kar raha hoon.

notes: Urdu for 'there is' = '___ hai' with location phrase before
Commands often use 'karo', 'khol do', 'band karo', 'jala do'

lines.urdu: میں کمرہ صاف کر رہا ہوں۔
lines.roman: Main kamra saaf kar raha hoon.

translate_to_urdu: There is a bed in the room.

notes: ‘Mera/Meri’ depends on gender of the noun being possessed
Family words have fixed gender; memorize them early
Descriptive adjectives come AFTER the noun

lines.urdu: آپ کے کتنے بہن بھائی ہیں؟
lines.roman: Aap ke kitne behen bhai hain?
lines.english: How many siblings do you have?

phrases.english: I wake up in the morning.

phrases.urdu: میں دوپہر میں کھانا کھاتا ہوں۔
phrases.roman: Main dopehar mein khana khata hoon.
phrases.english: I eat lunch in the afternoon.

notes: Present simple uses -ta/ti/te endings: jata, jati, jate
Time words (subah, shaam, raat) come at beginning

goals: Buy items with correct Urdu quantities

notes: "Kitne ka hai" = price question for masculine items

goals: Understand and say the time in Urdu
Use quarter, half, and hour expressions
Talk about your morning and night activities

phrases.english: I get up early in the morning.

goals: Talk about morning and evening habits

phrases.urdu: میں ہر روز صبح چائے پیتا ہوں۔
phrases.roman: Main har roz subah chai peeta hoon.

phrases.english: He takes a walk in the evening.

phrases.urdu: ہم اکثر شام کو ملتے ہیں۔
phrases.roman: Hum aksar shaam ko miltay hain.
phrases.english: We often meet in the evening.

points: Time-of-day markers go before the verb
Frequency words: har roz, aksar, kabhi kabhi

goals: Use future tense with 'گا / گی / گے'
